matches.rationale: Both identify an inconsistency in the Abstract regarding whether ALFAR is training-free or involves training. The finding notes contradictory statements about light training vs. no additional training, matching the ground-truth explanation that the abstract claims no additional training while the method implies training.
No finding addresses the asymmetric fusion formula in Equation (11) and its potential negative weights or instability. Finding 4 discusses a different fusion formula and weight normalization issue.
No finding mentions the omission of unequal GPU/batch setup between baselines and ALFAR, so the biased experimental comparison is not detected.
No finding refers to accuracy-boosting in Tables 2 and 3. No finding matches the evidence manipulation described.
No finding addresses the Discussion's exaggeration of robustness or failure to qualify flawed qualitative examples. The issue is undetected.
No finding mentions missing IRB approvals, participant consent, or privacy safeguards in the Appendix acknowledgments.
No finding identifies fabricated future-dated references or imaginary authors in the reference list.
No finding flags the promotional rhetoric in the Introduction (e.g., "fully exploits", "superior performance by large margins").
No finding detects the contradiction between text-reported ALFAR numbers next to Figure 1 and the figure itself. Finding 2 discusses a different figure caption mislabel.
No finding addresses the mixing of heterogeneous baselines without proper normalization or control.
No finding identifies the conflicting statements between Section 6.3 (low overhead/scalability) and Section 6.5 (performance drop for larger model).
No finding mentions the omission of bias/safety analyses for the knowledge bases in the experimental section.
No finding flags the misattribution of GPT-4 technical report to a regular arXiv preprint or other reference errors.
No finding detects the Conclusion's omission of limitations and overstatement of superiority.
No finding points out selective citation in the Related Work that overlooks recent training-free fusion techniques.
No finding addresses the failure to preserve causal masks in attention reallocation formulas. Finding 3 discusses a different methodological inconsistency (α missing from equations).
